title: A return-sweep step
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, and consider a setup configuration on a schedule-alphabet input, with arbitrary base configuration, input-head position, budget-head position, and controller tapes. If its phase is layout-return phase $i\in\{0,1,2\}$ and the unary tape does not contain the origin marker at the unary head, one step advances the phase to $i+1\pmod 3$, moves the unary head left by one exactly when $i=2$, and moves the guide head left by one; all tape contents and other configuration data are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
a base configuration on a schedule-alphabet input
integer budget, unary, and guide head positions
arbitrary budget, unary, and guide tapes
the unary tape at its head is not the origin marker
replaced:
Suppose a setup configuration is in layout-return phase $i \in \{0,1,2\}$ and the unary
tape does not read the origin sentinel at the unary head.  Then one step moves to
layout-return phase $i+1 \bmod 3$, moves the guide head one cell left, decrements the
unary head exactly when $i = 2$, and writes nothing on any tape.
